title: Day 0 - Primer
headline: CODEBREAKER'S PRIMER
subheadline: Training cipher for new agents. Work the five tells in order: single-letter words, frequent letters, short words, apostrophes, then double letters. Tap a glyph and type — every copy of that glyph fills at once.

title: Day 1 - Easy
headline: TRAGEDY AT THE VANCE ESTATE
subheadline: High society was rocked last night when Archibald Vance, the renowned railroad and shipping tycoon, was discovered deceased in his locked study during his annual gala. Thorne noted the absence of a weapon, yet a distinct scent of bitter almonds lingered in the air. A drafted telegraph addressed to the District Attorney—Vance’s final ultimatum threatening to burn down his partner's empire—was recovered from Vance's tuxedo pocket. Was it suicide, or did someone poison Vance’s champagne before he could pull the trigger on his threats?

title: Day 1 - Hard
headline: SILENCED BEFORE DAWN
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The drafted telegraph in Vance’s tuxedo pocket was not a whistleblower’s confession. It was a final ultimatum to the District Attorney, threatening to burn Sterling’s empire unless Vance kept control of the syndicate. Police now believe he was silenced before he could send it. Decode this late-city transmission before the trail goes cold.

title: Day 2 - Easy
headline: THE WIDOW'S LAMENT
subheadline: I interviewed Beatrice Vance this morning. The grieving widow was dressed in immaculate black silk, her eyes dry and her demeanor as cold as ice. She claims she was dancing with her husband's business partner, Arthur Sterling, at the exact time of the murder. But the upstairs maid confided in me that Beatrice and Archibald had a screaming match just hours before the guests arrived. Beatrice was demanding the combination to the wall safe, screaming that she wouldn't be left penniless. I found a charred scrap of paper near the fireplace in Beatrice's boudoir. It seems the flames didn't quite finish their job hiding her secrets.

title: Day 2 - Hard
headline: THE RED SAILBOAT
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — After the widow’s morning interview, detectives forced the library at dusk. Behind a painting of a crimson sailboat they found a scorched fragment of a safe combination, written in cipher. Beatrice Vance has left the estate. This night extra contains the remaining encoded lines recovered from the frame.

title: Day 3 - Easy
headline: A MISSING HEIR
subheadline: Whispers echo through the hallowed halls of the Vance estate today following the reading of the late millionaire’s will. While Arthur Sterling and the widow Beatrice sat stiffly in the parlor, the lawyer revealed a shocking twist. The bulk of the massive fortune was not left to the charming Mrs. Vance, but to Archibald’s estranged daughter, Clara, who vanished under mysterious circumstances three years ago! The room erupted into chaos, and Sterling abruptly left the premises. Our sources indicate a frantic search is underway. Why did Sterling look so terrified at the mention of Clara’s name? Meanwhile, authorities received an unsigned postcard today, bearing nothing but garbled text.

title: Day 3 - Hard
headline: SHE WAS SENT AWAY
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The morning rumor that Clara Vance still lives has been overtaken by a darker lead. A night clerk at Grand Central sold detectives a ticket stub to an upstate sanatorium, purchased in Arthur Sterling’s name. This late dispatch, intercepted from a private courier, explains why she vanished three years ago.

title: Day 4 - Easy
headline: SHADOWS IN THE OFFICE
subheadline: A midnight call roused me from what little slumber I had managed since the gala. Sterling’s East Side boys broke into the Vance & Sterling Shipping Co. downtown. The night guard was knocked unconscious, and Vance’s private office was tossed. Curiously, they weren't after cash—the company safe was untouched, though it bears fresh scratch marks. Instead, the heavy filing cabinets containing the maritime logs from 1923 were emptied. That is the exact year Clara Vance supposedly ran away. Whatever Sterling is hiding, it involves those ships. On the floor beneath the shattered window, I found a train ticket stub to Albany—Sterling’s men coordinating with someone upstate. No rest for the wicked, or the men hunting them. Written on the back was a hastily scrawled coded message.

title: Day 4 - Hard
headline: CONTRABAND ON THE RUNNER
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The morning raid on Vance & Sterling’s office was only the opening. Harbor watchmen now swear The Midnight Runner takes on unmarked crates after the lights go out. A second cipher, found in the emptied maritime logs, names both the illicit cargo and a daughter who knows too much.

title: Day 5 - Easy
headline: AN INTERCEPTED WIRE
subheadline: A stroke of luck. Our boys down at the telegraph office intercepted a message sent by Arthur Sterling to a mysterious "Mr. Black" at a private club in Albany. Sterling has been sweating bullets since the will reading, pacing his study until all hours of the night. Beatrice Vance has also been seen entering Sterling’s estate through the servant's entrance. The web of deception grows thicker. Are the widow and the business partner working together, or are they circling each other like vultures? The telegraph operator managed to copy down two segments of the transmission before the line was suspiciously cut. We must decode these immediately.

title: Day 5 - Hard
headline: THE WIDOW'S PRICE
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Sterling’s intercepted wire was only the first page. A second transmission, cut off when the line went dead at 11:47 p.m., suggests Beatrice Vance knows about the poison and is demanding payment to stay silent. Decode this night extra before she vanishes with the evidence.

title: Day 6 - Easy
headline: THE DOCTOR'S SECRET
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 9, 1926)
Three days on nothing but black coffee, Lucky Strikes, and a sleeping car to Albany. I stumbled off the platform in a rumpled suit, eyes bloodshot, following the ticket stub trail to the Blackwood Sanatorium. The head physician, Dr. Aris Blackwood, was remarkably uncooperative. He insisted patient records were strictly confidential. However, a sympathetic nurse slipped me a folded napkin as I left the grounds. It seems Clara Vance was here, registered under an assumed name, but she escaped the Sunday before her father’s murder. The nurse whispered that the widow had Sterling arrange to lock her away rather than put her in the ground—flesh and blood, after all. Dr. Blackwood has been receiving hefty monthly payments from Vance & Sterling Shipping Co. to keep her drugged and silent. The nurse’s note contained two coded messages, likely passed between the doctor and his mysterious benefactors.

title: Day 6 - Hard
headline: DRUGGED TO SILENCE
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The nurse’s napkin was not the last word from Blackwood Sanatorium. After dark, a second note was slipped under Detective Thorne’s hotel door: Clara had been kept insensible to stop her from naming the bootlegging routes. This cipher is the doctor’s own hand.

title: Day 7 - Easy
headline: THE MIDNIGHT RUNNER
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The Waterfront Whisperer, Sept 10, 1926)
A suspicious vessel, The Midnight Runner, was raided by the Coast Guard late last night in the harbor. Registered to Vance & Sterling Shipping Co., the cargo manifest claimed it was transporting textiles from Cuba. However, underneath the crates of silk, authorities uncovered hundreds of crates of premium Canadian whiskey! Witnesses say Detective Elias Thorne, still in yesterday’s rumpled suit and looking as though he had not slept since Albany, was already on the pier when the boarding party went over the rail. Rumors are swirling that Archibald Vance discovered the illegal use of his ships and threatened to expose the whole operation. Was he murdered to protect a million-dollar bootlegging empire? A cryptic ledger was found in the captain’s quarters, containing encoded entries that point fingers at high society.

title: Day 7 - Hard
headline: FAKE MANIFESTS
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Coast Guard papers seized from The Midnight Runner include a second ledger page the morning edition did not print. Vance had discovered the forged manifests and threatened to burn the fleet. Someone silenced him first. The captain’s cipher names the reason.

title: Day 8 - Easy
headline: THE BUTLER'S CONFESSION
subheadline:
(Police Interrogation Transcript - Sept 11, 1926)
I brought Reginald, the Vance family butler, in for questioning today. He has served the family for twenty years but looked as though he had aged a decade overnight. He finally broke under pressure, admitting he used his master key on the locked study minutes before Archibald Vance was found dead. As the oak door swung in, he caught the scent of expensive French perfume. He was paid handsomely to turn that key and forget who walked through. When asked who paid him, Reginald refused to speak, terrified for his life. A search of his quarters turned up a roll of fifty-dollar bills and a matchbook from a notorious downtown speakeasy, The Blind Tiger, with a message scrawled inside.

title: Day 8 - Hard
headline: SHE DID NOT ACT ALONE
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The butler’s daylight confession of French perfume and a turned master key was incomplete. Under lamplight at headquarters he recanted part of his story and whispered a longer cipher: the widow delivered the poison, but another hand was in the room. This night extra is his true statement.

title: Day 9 - Easy
headline: SECRETS IN THE SAFE
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 12, 1926)
Using the clue decoded from Beatrice’s note, I located the hidden wall safe behind the red sailboat painting. Inside lay an explosive collection of blackmail files, and a hidden birth certificate: Clara was born out of wedlock to Beatrice long before her marriage to Vance. Archibald had officially 'adopted' Clara as a stepdaughter to bury the scandal, but Beatrice despised the girl as a living reminder of her past. That is why Clara went to a sanatorium instead of a grave.

title: Day 9 - Hard
headline: BLACKMAIL IN THE PRESS
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The wall safe yielded more than blackmail. A midnight inventory produced a second encoded letter in Clara’s hand, threatening to take a blackmail ring to the newspapers unless her father ended it. The morning paper held back this dispatch at the Bureau’s request.

title: Day 10 - Easy
headline: A VOICE FROM THE SHADOWS
subheadline:
(Intercepted Letter - Sept 13, 1926)
A letter arrived at the precinct today, addressed directly to me. It smelled faintly of lavender and damp earth. The handwriting was elegant but frantic. It was from Clara Vance. She reveals she is hiding in plain sight in the city, terrified for her life. She claims her father’s death was just the beginning, and that The Blind Tiger is the center of the conspiracy. She watched from a priest-hole behind the bookshelves, but the angle was cruel: she could see only hands, a distinctive silver cane, and hear a deep voice. The sanatorium narcotics have left her memory in fragments. The man’s face is a blur. She enclosed two ciphers, promising they hold the key to the killer's identity.

title: Day 10 - Hard
headline: THE WIDOW AND THE CANE
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — “Find the silver cane” was only the first line. A second letter arrived after dusk, describing Arthur Sterling’s limp — and the widow carrying his cane through the study. Clara still cannot name the man with the deep voice. This night extra may identify who held the cane, and who poured the glass.

title: Day 11 - Easy
headline: INTO THE TIGER'S DEN
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 14, 1926)
Following the matchbook clue, I traded my detective's coat for a cheap suit and slinked into The Blind Tiger. The speakeasy was thick with cigar smoke, bathtub gin, and the frantic rhythm of a ragtime band. Through the haze, I spotted Arthur Sterling tucked away in a velvet VIP booth, sweating profusely while negotiating with two known enforcers from the East Side mob. The bartender was acting as their go-between, passing folded notes under cocktail napkins. I managed to swipe one of the napkins when a scuffle broke out by the roulette table. The criminal underground is firmly embedded in Vance's shipping empire, and these ciphers prove it.

title: Day 11 - Hard
headline: PAYOFFS AT THE BAR
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Sterling’s meeting with the mob was confirmed after closing time. A bartender who “serves more than drinks” distributes dock payoffs from behind the rail. This late cipher, recovered from a napkin ring, names the go-between.

title: Day 12 - Easy
headline: THE HOLLOW CANE
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The New York Chronicle, Sept 15, 1926)
A major breakthrough in the Vance murder case! Spurred by the precinct's published reward notice, a local pawnshop owner stepped forward this morning with a silver-handled cane matching our description. The owner claims a woman draped in black veils pawned the item for a fraction of its worth just hours after Archibald Vance was discovered dead. Upon police inspection, the cane was revealed to be hollow, housing a removable glass vial. Residual tests confirmed the presence of bitter almonds—liquid cyanide. This was no murder weapon left at the scene. It was a smuggling vessel, used to walk poison past gala security. Beatrice pawned it in a panic because the residue would hang her. Whispers in the precinct say she later claimed Sterling had the cane all night.

title: Day 12 - Hard
headline: THE SMUGGLER'S CANE
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The silver cane was never meant to be left beside the body. Night chemists confirmed a hidden vial: Beatrice stole it from Arthur to walk the cyanide into the gala undetected, then pawned it when the residue terrified her. The morning edition could not print this without the decoded proof.

title: Day 13 - Easy
headline: AN EMPTY ROOM
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 16, 1926)
Using the postmarks from Clara's letter, I tracked her hideout to a run-down boarding house in the Bowery. I was too late. The door hung off its hinges, and the small room had been violently tossed. A shattered mirror and a knocked-over chair pointed to a desperate struggle. Clara Vance has been taken. On the remaining shards of the vanity mirror, someone—likely Clara in her final moments before capture—had hastily scrawled a message using red lipstick. The implications of this code are staggering. If this is true, the rot in this city goes much higher than a shipping company.

title: Day 13 - Hard
headline: THE MAYOR ORDERED THE RAID
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Clara’s boarding-house room was empty by moonrise, but she left a longer warning than “they found me.” The night extra names City Hall: the Mayor ordered the ship raid to bury his own tracks. Decode it before the next knock at the door.

title: Day 14 - Easy
headline: A GRUESOME DISCOVERY
subheadline:
(Police Evidence File - September 17, 1926)
A body was pulled from the East River at dawn. My stomach dropped, fearing it was Clara, but the victim was identified as Reginald, the Vance family butler. His pockets were weighed down with cobblestones, a classic mob execution. Attached to his suspenders was a waterproof oilskin pouch. Inside, we found a torn page from Archibald Vance’s private ledger—the master book he kept in the study, not the 1923 maritime files Sterling’s men emptied downtown. Reginald found it on the desk after he unlocked the door, swiped it before the cops arrived, and tried to squeeze the mob for more money. They decided to permanently silence him. The ledger page contains shipping coordinates and a terrifying cipher that changes everything we know about the smuggling ring.

title: Day 14 - Hard
headline: WEAPONS IN THE HOLD
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The gruesome waterfront discovery was not the downtown 1923 files. A second page from Archibald’s private study ledger, withheld from the morning run, indicates Sterling was moving arms with the Canadian spirits. This cipher is the missing inventory.

title: Day 15 - Easy
headline: THE MAYOR STEPS DOWN
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The Long Island Tattler, Sept 18, 1926)
In a shocking morning press conference, Mayor H. Harrison announced his immediate resignation, citing "sudden and severe health reasons." The city is buzzing with speculation, but our precinct knows the truth. Detective Thorne raided the Mayor’s private office just as the movers were packing his mahogany desk. Hidden in the false bottom of a cigar humidor, Thorne discovered the blackmail materials Archibald Vance had been using to bleed the Mayor dry. Vance had him in a vice grip, and the Mayor had every reason to want him dead. Thorne has submitted two coded threats from Vance to the lab for decryption.

title: Day 15 - Hard
headline: DO NOT TRUST THE UNIFORM
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The Mayor’s resignation was the daylight story. After dark, a second threat arrived: the Police Chief is on the same payroll. This late-city cipher warns the public not to trust anyone in blue until it is decoded.

title: Day 16 - Easy
headline: THE CHIEF'S DILEMMA
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 19, 1926)
With the Mayor stepping down and the Police Chief implicated in the blackmail ring, I realize I cannot trust my own department. I am entirely on my own. Last night, I broke into the Chief’s private office, searching for any indication of where Clara Vance might have been taken. The corrupt Chief had been feeding information directly to the mob—and now he intends to finish the job himself. Under his blotter, I discovered a carbon copy of a secretly intercepted telegraph message, routed away from my desk. It contained coordinates and a chilling deadline. The Chief is assembling a crooked hit squad. They are holding Clara somewhere on the waterfront, and they plan to silence her tonight.

title: Day 16 - Hard
headline: MIDNIGHT AT PIER FORTY FOUR
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — “Trust no one in blue” was the morning caution. A night courier brought coordinates: Clara is held in an abandoned warehouse on Pier 44, and the Police Chief himself is riding out at midnight to make sure she never talks. This extra may be her last chance.

title: Day 17 - Easy
headline: SHOOTOUT AT PIER 44
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The Waterfront Whisperer, Sept 20, 1926)
Gunfire shattered the midnight quiet at Pier 44! A lone, rogue detective engaged in a fierce shootout with a crooked hit squad led by the Police Chief himself. When the smoke cleared in the fog, the Chief lay dead on the planks—dropped by Detective Thorne’s revolver—and the remaining badges had fled into the night, leaving behind a terrified but unharmed Clara Vance. The missing heiress has finally been found! Thorne escorted her to a secure, undisclosed location. There is no going back to the force now. Rumors say Clara has agreed to testify about the night of her father's murder, and what she witnessed from the secret passage in his study changes the entire investigation. She carried two coded notes she stole from her captors.

title: Day 17 - Hard
headline: BOOTLEGGER, NOT KILLER
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The Police Chief is dead in the fog, but the shootout left a second statement on the warehouse floor. Sterling was at The Blind Tiger during the murder—a bootlegger, not the killer. Beatrice had lifted his silver cane from the estate after their screaming match, having Dr. Blackwood fill it with cyanide so she could smuggle it into the gala. Sterling kept the empty vial as insurance once he realized he was being framed.

title: Day 18 - Easy
headline: THE DAUGHTER'S TALE
subheadline:
(Police Interrogation Transcript - Sept 21, 1926)
Clara sat trembling, drinking black coffee. "I was hiding in the priest-hole behind the bookshelves," she whispered. "The boards cut the room in half. I could see hands. I could see the silver cane. I heard a deep voice. I could not see his face." The sanatorium narcotics have left her memory in pieces—dread without a name. "My father was threatening to burn Sterling's smuggling ships, yes, but Arthur wasn't there that night. It was Beatrice—my own mother. She wasn't alone." Archibald had locked the heavy oak doors from inside. Then the master key turned. Reginald, the butler, let them in. Through the slats she watched Beatrice hand him the fatal glass while the deep voice issued threats from the shadows. The killers wiped the glass and slipped out. Clara hastily sketched two ciphers from what little she could swear to.

title: Day 18 - Hard
headline: TWO IN THE STUDY
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — Clara’s morning testimony named two killers, and the butler who turned the master key. After dusk she dictated a longer cipher: she saw the silver cane and heard a deep voice, but the priest-hole and the drugs stole the man’s face. Archibald died because he underestimated his own servant. This night extra is her full account.

title: Day 19 - Easy
headline: THE DOCTOR RETURNS
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 22, 1926)
A deep voice. A silver cane. A face Clara could not name. I brought in an abandoned medical bag retrieved from the Albany line and opened the latches. The sharp, clinical stench of sanatorium narcotics hit the room. Clara’s hands began to shake violently—the sensory shock tore through the drug haze. 'That smell... that voice.' Passenger manifests confirmed Dr. Aris Blackwood arrived in New York hours before the gala.

title: Day 19 - Hard
headline: CYANIDE IN THE BAG
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The medical bag that tore through Clara’s haze also named the method. A night search produced a second cipher: he supplied the cyanide and filled the hollow cane Beatrice had stolen from the estate, a smuggling vessel, not a calling card left beside the corpse. The morning edition lacked this charge.

title: Day 20 - Easy
headline: LOVERS ON THE RUN
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The New York Chronicle, Sept 23, 1926)
A city-wide manhunt is underway for socialite Beatrice Vance and Dr. Aris Blackwood. Detective Thorne breached Beatrice's Plaza Hotel suite this morning to find the wall safe emptied. A terrified maid reported seeing the pair fleeing toward the harbor, noting the doctor looked pale and frantic while Beatrice stared at him with cold, predatory eyes. The murderous lovers have fled, leaving behind a coded note.

title: Day 20 - Hard
headline: STOP THE HAVANA STEAMER
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The lovers fled the Plaza by daylight. Harbor pilots now report a steamer clearing for Havana with a leather trunk in the hold. This night extra is the stop-order Thorne wired to the docks — still in cipher.

title: Day 21 - Easy
headline: THE BAIT IS SET
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 24, 1926)
With the local police force hopelessly compromised—and my own Chief dead by my hand at Pier 44—Clara and I cannot simply walk into a precinct. We need the rats to eat each other. I leaked two rumors through a trusted dockworker: to Sterling, that Clara has her father's original bootlegging ledger; to Beatrice, that the Mayor’s untaxed gold is moving at midnight through Pier 84. They will both come armed, each expecting to collect. I also timed a tip to the Treasury boys—not to save me, but to sweep the boards after the blood is on the planks. We arranged the meeting at the abandoned pier. I only hope their greed outweighs their caution. Two encoded messages were sent via courier to ensure the trap is sprung.

title: Day 21 - Hard
headline: HE WILL BRING HIS GUNS
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The trap at Pier 84 is set. A second courier slip, sent after the morning rumor, claims Sterling believes they have the ledger and will come with his guns. Beatrice is coming for the gold. Decode this night dispatch before the lantern is lit.

title: Day 22 - Easy
headline: A SHOCKING ARRIVAL
subheadline:
(Police Evidence File - Narrative Account, Sept 25, 1926)
The trap at Pier 84 was set. Clara stood nervously by a single flickering lantern, clutching a decoy ledger. I was perched high above in the rusted iron rafters, my revolver drawn. A sleek black Packard silently rolled onto the damp wooden docks. The door opened, but it wasn't Arthur Sterling who stepped out. It was Beatrice Vance, wrapped in mink and holding a pearl-handled Derringer. Through the window I caught Dr. Aris Blackwood slumped in the passenger seat, his head at an angle no living man could hold. Beatrice laughed. She had no intention of splitting the fortune with a sanatorium doctor—or with anyone. Aiming the gun at Clara, she whispered that three years in a padded room had been mercy, the most a mother could stomach. Tonight the gold was thicker than blood.

title: Day 22 - Hard
headline: SHE PLAYED THEM ALL
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — It was not Sterling who stepped from the Packard. Beatrice Vance arrived with a Derringer, a dead doctor in the passenger seat, and a confession: she spared her own daughter once with a sanatorium, then decided a million in gold was thicker than blood. This night extra is the longer statement taken on the dock.

title: Day 23 - Easy
headline: HONOR AMONG THIEVES
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 26, 1926)
Before Beatrice could pull the trigger, I dropped a flash flare from the rafters, allowing Clara to scramble behind heavy iron freight crates as the shadows around the Packard shifted. Arthur Sterling stepped forward with his hired guns, exactly as I had baited him. He knew someone was setting a trap, but he allowed Beatrice to walk into it first, using her as a shield. The two crews instantly turned on each other, which was the entire point. Sterling revealed he had secretly kept the empty poison vial Beatrice used to murder her husband, intending to frame her if the police ever closed in. Mob enforcers and Beatrice’s remaining muscle melted out of the fog, surrounding both of them, guns drawn. I stayed in the rafters and let the wolves work. A terrifying Mexican standoff ensued on the rotting planks of the pier.

title: Day 23 - Hard
headline: THE VIAL IN HIS POCKET
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Honor among thieves lasted until moonrise. Sterling produced the empty poison vial and moved to kill Beatrice, pinning every murder on her. Mob guns are still drawn. This cipher is what Thorne overheard from the rafters.

title: Day 24 - Easy
headline: AFTER THE BLOOD
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The New York Chronicle, Sept 27, 1926)
By the time the sirens reached Pier 84, the wolves had already torn each other apart in the midnight fog. Detective Thorne did not call for cavalry. He arranged the meeting so Sterling’s mob and Beatrice’s hired guns would do the killing for him, then sat in the rafters until the shooting slowed. Only then did his timed tip bring the Treasury Department—cleanup men, hungry for the Mayor’s untaxed gold, not saviors. Beatrice Vance dropped what was left of her Derringer and wept for a lawyer. Arthur Sterling attempted to sprint toward a waiting speedboat, but Thorne finally came down from the iron and tackled him to the dock, sending his loaded revolver plunging into the dark waters of the Hudson River. The reign of the Vance & Sterling crime syndicate has violently ended.

title: Day 24 - Hard
headline: THE FIGHT IS NOT OVER
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — Thorne let the crews butcher each other before Treasury arrived as the cleanup. Sterling’s arrest is not the last chapter. Enforcers are in irons; the syndicate’s remaining accounts are still encoded. This night extra warns that the fight continues downtown.

title: Day 25 - Easy
headline: A CONFESSION UNDER NEON
subheadline:
(Police Interrogation Transcript - Federal Bureau, Sept 28, 1926)
Sitting under the buzzing lights of a federal interrogation room, Arthur Sterling finally broke. With his mob muscle locked up and his corrupt police contacts facing federal indictments, he had no protection left to hide behind. Sweating and trembling, he confessed that Archibald Vance was preparing to expose the syndicate to the District Attorney to seize sole control. Beatrice, terrified of losing her lavish lifestyle and social standing, approached Sterling with the cyanide. They plotted the murder together to protect their wealth. From behind the darkened observation window, Clara Vance stood beside me, watching the man who destroyed her family finally face justice.

title: Day 25 - Hard
headline: THE CHAIR AWAITS
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Sterling signed by daylight. After the lights dimmed in the interrogation room he added a second cipher: the conspiracy is broken, and the guilty face the electric chair. Clara watched from behind the glass as this night post went to type.

title: Day 26 - Easy
headline: THE WIDOW'S LAST STAND
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The Waterfront Whisperer, Sept 29, 1926)
In federal custody, Beatrice Vance attempted one final, desperate play. She tried to seduce the federal prosecutor, offering him the location of a hidden off-shore vault containing a million dollars in gold bullion if he would drop her charges and pin the mastermind label solely on Sterling. The prosecutor, unswayed, recorded the entire conversation. Detective Thorne used the coordinates Beatrice foolishly revealed to locate the vault, securing the stolen wealth for the Vance estate. The trial of the century begins tomorrow, and the city's corrupt elite are trembling as subpoenas are handed out like candy.

title: Day 26 - Hard
headline: GOLD FOR THE HEIR
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — Beatrice’s bribe failed, and the offshore vault is located. A night inventory cipher confirms the bullion returns to the rightful heir, and the widow will rot in prison. The morning paper printed the attempt; this extra prints the sentence.

title: Day 27 - Easy
headline: THE TRIAL OF THE CENTURY
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 30, 1926)
The supreme court gallery was packed to the rafters as the joint capital murder trial of Arthur Sterling and Beatrice Vance commenced. Photographers' flashbulbs popped like firecrackers as Clara Vance took the witness stand. Dressed in a modest navy suit, she recounted her father’s murder and her harrowing abduction with a poise that won over the jury instantly. Sterling’s high-priced attorneys attempted to poke holes in my rogue investigation, but the federal prosecutor introduced the decoded bootlegging ledger as exhibit A. The jury deliberated for less than an hour. The hammer of justice has finally fallen on the Vance and Sterling syndicate.

title: Day 27 - Hard
headline: THE EMPIRE IS CRUSHED
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The jury was out less than an hour. A second encoded note from the prosecutor’s table records what the morning extras could not: the defense’s lies did not take, and the bootlegging empire is crushed. Late city final.

title: Day 28 - Easy
headline: THE SECRET INHERITANCE
subheadline:
(Police Evidence File - Narrative Account, Oct 1, 1926)
With the gavel falling on Beatrice, Clara Vance finally returned to her father's sprawling Long Island estate. Escorted by Detective Thorne, she met with Archibald's private attorney. It turns out, Archibald knew his life was in danger long before the gala. He had quietly transferred the majority of his legitimate assets, real estate, and shipping patents into a blind trust solely in Clara's name. Beatrice never stood a chance at inheriting the empire, even if her murderous plot had succeeded without a hitch. Among the legal documents, Thorne found two final cryptograms left by Archibald himself.

title: Day 28 - Hard
headline: HE KNEW THEY WOULD BETRAY HIM
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — Archibald’s blind trust was the daylight miracle. Among his papers Thorne found a longer cipher in the dead man’s hand: he knew they were plotting, and he locked the fortune beyond their greed. This is his last night letter.

title: Day 29 - Easy
headline: A NEW DAWN
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The New York Chronicle, Oct 2, 1926)
A crisp autumn wind blew off the harbor as Clara Vance stood before the headquarters of the newly renamed Vance Maritime Company. Her first act as sole proprietor was to fire every dock manager, accountant, and captain with ties to Arthur Sterling's illegal operations. She dismantled the bootlegging empire overnight, replacing the corrupt fleet with honest crews and legitimate cargo manifests. Detective Thorne watched from the docks as the first clean ships set sail. The rot looked cut out of New York. Thorne’s smile did not quite reach his eyes. There were still a few lines left in his journal.

title: Day 29 - Hard
headline: SHE KEPT THE SECRETS
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Clean ships left the harbor at dawn, but Thorne’s journal held a second cipher for the late run. He had watched Clara lock her father’s blackmail files in her own safe rather than burn them. She fired the bootleggers, but she kept the secrets. In this city, an honest woman still needs fangs.

title: Day 30 - Easy
headline: CASE CLOSED
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Oct 3, 1926)
I sit in my favorite diner, watching the rain wash the city streets clean. The Vance case is officially closed. Arthur Sterling and Beatrice Vance sit in Sing Sing’s death cells awaiting the electric chair, and Mayor Harrison’s corrupt administration is nothing but a disgraced memory. My badge sits in a drawer. After Pier 44, there is no precinct that would have me, and none I would have back. Before she left for a tour of Europe, Clara Vance sent me a parting gift: a gold pocket watch engraved with my name, and a small envelope containing two final ciphers. It’s a quiet morning. New York feels safer. I know better than to call it honest.

title: Day 30 - Hard
headline: A DETECTIVE NEVER FORGETS
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The diner was quiet this morning. Clara’s last envelope, opened under the night lamps of the Chronicle composing room, contains a longer farewell: Thorne is a true detective, and her family will not forget this autumn. Case closed — night extra.
